headline: US has 'effectively blocked' Iranian oil exports via Hormuz
dek: Washington has 'effectively blocked' Iranian oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz while 13-14 million barrels/day from other countries transit with US military escort/protection; 'The only country in the world that cannot get a single barrel of oil through the Straits of Hormuz is Iran'; flow…
sources: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Breitbart News interview (State Dept release)
fault_line: Strangling Iran's economy without breaking global supply — or a blockade that forces Tehran's next move?

sections.what_happened: Washington has 'effectively blocked' Iranian oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz while 13-14 million barrels/day from other countries transit with US military escort/protection; 'The only country in the world that cannot get a single barrel of oil through the Straits of Hormuz is Iran'; flow volumes 'equivalent to what it was pre-conflict' some days.
sections.what_verified: Trump's own Truth Social posts on US naval blockade of Iran (covered in 10-19 scans); Centcom strike claims re Hormuz shipping. No independent verification of the '13-14M bbl/day' figures — Rubio himself presented them as administration assessment.
sections.what_disputed: Iran denies it has lost control of the strait; IRGC Navy says Hormuz closed until US lifts port blockade; Iran claims it can still move oil via 'shadow' arrangements. No independent shipping data published to confirm volumes.
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook + energy-war explainer: US claims a surgical economic strangulation of Iran that keeps the world's oil flowing — with map of Hormuz and barrel counts; skeptical note that the figures are Washington's own, unverified.
sections.context: Background: Rubio: US has 'effectively blocked' Iranian oil exports via Hormuz; 13-14M bbl/day for others escorted by US forces

totw_analysis: Our read: Pocketbook + energy-war explainer: US claims a surgical economic strangulation of Iran that keeps the world's oil flowing — with map of Hormuz and barrel counts; skeptical note that the figures are Washington's own, unverified. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Strangling Iran's economy without breaking global supply — or a blockade that forces Tehran's next move?
